title: GPU capacity thresholds & rebalance proposals — weekly sync
content:
Purpose:
This is the working capture from today's weekly infra sync focused on GPU capacity thresholds, regional rebalance proposals, and immediate operational steps. Intended audience: Capacity owners, ops oncall, and platform engineers who touch scheduling and routing.

Meeting notes (2026-05-27):
- Attendees: Anika (chair), Marco, Ethan, Zoe, oncall-1 (rotation), data-ops observer
- Quick status: overall cluster utilization 68% across prod regions (past 7d avg). Edge regions (us-west-2-edge / eu-west-1-edge) are at 82% during 18:00-02:00 local peaks. Latency SLO breach observed in eu-west-1 on 5/25 (minute-scale tail spikes) — incident follow-up links below.

Capacity thresholds rationale:
- Goal: enforce soft thresholds per region to preserve 10–15% headroom for burst and backfill.
- Proposal A (conservative): set per-region soft threshold at 78% (alert when >78% sustained for 10m), hard throttle at 92% with automatic spill to Dedicated pool.
- Proposal B (aggressive cost-first): set soft at 85%, hard at 95% with preemptible backfill allowed and priority demotion of non-SLA tenants.
- Observations: Edge regions have higher variance; Proposal A reduces risk of tail latency but increases cross-region routing. Proposal B saves cost but increases chance of user-facing retries.

Rebalance heuristics discussed:
- Use weighted multipliers for model memory density and avg seq len per workload. Models flagged in routing as "large-kv" get extra headroom buffer.
- Suggest adding a short-circuit: if region queue length > X and tail latency > Y, immediately route new sessions to nearest healthy region (use config: routing.fallback.rules).
- Consider rotating warm pools (short prewarming) for top 3 models by qps in each region to reduce cold-start spikes during rebalance.

Data / metrics snapshot (key signals):
- 7d avg GPU util: prod-global 68%
- Peak sustained util (us-west-2-edge): 82% (18:00–02:00)
- Tail p99.9 latency (eu-west-1) increased to 1.9s on 2026-05-25 incident window (baseline 1.1s)
- Backfill success rate: 96.7% (but longer queue times for preemptible jobs in high-util windows)

Action items (owner -> due):
1) Add soft/hard threshold config to infra flags and expose to console: implement Proposal A by default; make Proposal B an opt-in (Anika -> 2026-06-03).
2) Create a small simulation harness to run weekend traffic replays for Proposal A vs B for ring regions: generate delta report (Marco -> 2026-05-31).
3) Implement quick fallback rule: routing.fallback.rules -> add queue-length short-circuit in next deploy (Ethan -> 2026-06-01).
4) Warm-pool experiment: schedule 30m warm-pools for top-3 models in us-west-2-edge for weekday evenings; measure p99.9 delta (Zoe -> 2026-06-07).
5) Incident postmortem link + remediation checklist to be attached in Confluence (owner: oncall-1 -> 2026-05-29).

Decisions made during sync:
- We will move forward with Proposal A as the conservative baseline for the next two weeks while running the simulation for Proposal B.
- Any region-specific harder thresholds (lower than 78%) will require sign-off from the regional product owner.

Open questions / risks:
- Risk: cross-region routing increases egress costs and may introduce higher latencies if network path unstable. Need to quantify typical reroute latency overhead per region pair.
- Question: should we auto-scale dedicated fallback or use manual approvals for bursts beyond 92%? (defer to biz ops for cost estimate).
- Risk: warm-pool policy could increase idle-hours GPU spend; need to cap by time window and model impact.

Notes-to-self / quick checklist for rollout:
- Update infra feature flag docs (infra/flags/capacity-thresholds) with default values and toggle instructions.
- Add dashboards: per-region util + calendar heatmap + reroute events overlay; include a numeric headroom gauge.
- Add smoke-test to deploy pipeline that forces a simulated high-queue to validate fallback rule.

Links / artifacts referenced:
- JIRA-1897: "eu-west-1 tail latency spike 5/25"
- JIRA-1902: "capacity-threshold-feature-flag"
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/842 (routing fallback draft)
- Confluence draft: confluence://infra/capacity-threshold-models

Retro notes (quick):
- Good: ops team flagged the eu-west-1 anomaly early; oncall runbook was followed and rollback avoided.
- Improve: need more pre-deploy simulation coverage for peak patterns (evenings) and a better local-run harness for engineers to test rebalance locally.

Next sync agenda (2026-06-03):
- Review simulation results (Marco)
- Validate feature-flag PR and staging smoke (Ethan)
- Warm-pool experiment plan and expected metrics (Zoe)
- Cost estimate for dedicated fallback (finance + bizops invite)

If you see anything missing or want to change the thresholds before I open the proposal PR, ping me in #infra-capacity or add comments to JIRA-1902.
